notes:
Sources:

Population: INE BGRI 2021 (Base Geográfica de Referenciação de Informação), Portugal's official census statistical grid — https://mapas.ine.pt/download/index2021.phtml
Buildings: Overture Maps Foundation, pulled via depot's MapGen pipeline
Roads, runways/taxiways, water geometry: OpenStreetMap, via a Portugal extract (Geofabrik), also through depot
Map generation tooling: depot (github.com/Subway-Builder-Modded/depot)

Pipeline: Map geometry (buildings, roads, runways, bathymetry, PMTiles) was generated with depot's MapGen against a bounding box covering central Lisbon and the Tagus estuary. Residential demand comes directly from real BGRI 2021 population counts (N_INDIVIDUOS) per statistical subsection — reprojected from Portugal's national grid (EPSG:3763) to WGS84, clipped to the map's bounding box, and placed at each subsection's centroid (~4,284 points in-bbox with population > 0). Job-side demand has no equivalent real dataset behind it: it's estimated from ~41 hand-selected real Lisbon landmarks and districts, weighted by category (CBD, transit hubs, university, tourist areas, industrial zones, the airport). Commute flows connect each residential point to its nearest/highest-scoring job points via a distance-decay gravity model, with flow sizes allocated using an exact largest-remainder method so resident, job, and commute totals all conserve precisely (869,472 across all three) rather than approximately.

What the dropdowns don't capture: this is a genuinely mixed-provenance dataset, not uniformly real or synthetic — population is real government census data, but job counts and driving times are estimated. Job totals were scaled (~5.9×, from ~147k to ~869k) specifically to satisfy the requirement that every resident's commute terminates at a real job slot; that scaling reflects the schema's closed-system logic, not real employment statistics, so absolute job figures at any given landmark shouldn't be read as literal workforce counts. Driving times/distances are straight-line (haversine) distance × a fixed detour factor at an assumed average urban speed, not derived from a routing engine (e.g. OSRM) — the largest remaining fidelity gap in the dataset.

Vintages: BGRI population data is the 2021 Portuguese census (most recent available). OSM and Overture data reflect whatever was current when the map was generated, early September 2026.

Claude was used to help put the data togheter
